recognize_zh: 臉部嚴重疤痕與色素沉著、雙手指節殘缺變形與潰瘍（光敏感造成的毀損），牙齒在紫外光下發出粉紅螢光（erythrodontia），尿液紫外光下呈粉紅螢光（porphyrinuria），符合先天性紅血球生成性紫質症（congenital erythropoietic porphyria）。
features: Clinical photographs, not a microscopic image
Panel A: severe facial scarring and hyperpigmentation; hands with mutilating deformity, shortened digits, ulcers and crusts
Panel B: erythrodontia with reddish-pink fluorescence of teeth under UV light
Panel C: porphyrinuria with pink fluorescence of patient urine versus blue normal control under UV light
describe_en: Clinical photographs (Balwani and Desnick, Hematology 2012) show severe cutaneous photosensitivity with facial scarring and hyperpigmentation, and mutilating deformities of both hands with digit loss, ulceration and crusting, consistent with repeated blistering, infection and scarring. Under ultraviolet light, the teeth show pink-red fluorescence (erythrodontia), and the patient's urine fluoresces pink compared with the blue fluorescence of a normal control (porphyrinuria). Findings are consistent with congenital erythropoietic porphyria (Gunther disease) due to uroporphyrinogen III synthase deficiency, typically accompanied by hemolytic anemia and splenomegaly.

ddx.vs: HEP can mimic CEP clinically but shows elevated urine uroporphyrin/heptacarboxyl porphyrin with isocoproporphyrin in feces and homozygous UROD deficiency rather than type I isomer predominance from UROS deficiency.
PCT presents in adulthood with milder blistering of the hands, without erythrodontia, hemolysis or mutilating deformity.
EPP causes painful non-blistering photosensitivity with normal urine porphyrins and no erythrodontia.
Dystrophic EB causes scarring and digit fusion but is trauma-related, without photosensitivity, fluorescent teeth or porphyrinuria.
